data.content_ref: inline:The isolated artifact ABSTRACTS away from every neighbourhood mechanism (mean principle, counterexample rejection, arithmetic-progression formula, exhaustive parity search) to a higher-order claim: the solution is determined not by any particular algebraic move but by a Galois-style closure — the set of constraints {3-term, evenly-spaced, sum=138} generates a closure system whose fixed point is a singleton set {(44,46,48)}. The neighbourhood artifacts each name one operator inside the closure (mean, parity-check, stride, counterexample); the isolated artifact names the closure itself as the mechanism. REFUTED IF the isolated artifact's derivation can be identified with any single neighbourhood mechanism — because then it does not abstract above them but merely restates one. REFUTED IF no neighbourhood artifact's counterconditions can be re-expressed as 'a constraint violation that breaks closure uniqueness' — because then the closure framing adds no explanatory power beyond the individual mechanisms it claims to abstract over. This is compatible with all neighbourhood conclusions (all yield 48) but subsumes their methods under one meta-principle.
